review.notes: Conflicting evidence recorded, not resolved: the pinned modern cards.cdb text equals lineage v0 (SDY-049, 2002-03-29) — the same text the goat entry carries — even though the lineage's newest English version is v1 (YSD-EN033, Starter Deck 2006, 2006-03-23: 'Increase the DEF of 1 face-up monster on the field by 500 points until the end of this turn'), so BabelCDB's English text lags the printed lineage. Nothing behavioural rides on that: both scripts already restrict the target to a face-up monster with DEF >= 0 and reset at the end of the turn, so v1 only codifies what both implement, which is why no text change is recorded. Rule-profile check: the GOAT profile's damage-step flags (DUEL_6_STEP_BATLLE_STEP, DUEL_SINGLE_CHAIN_IN_DAMAGE_SUBSTEP) do not decide per-effect activation windows, so this variant is not engine-redundant.

event.historical_text: Increase a selected monster's DEF by 500 points during the turn this card is activated.
event.summary: Era damage-step legality with no text change: the goat script carries EFFECT_FLAG_DAMAGE_CAL where the modern script carries EFFECT_FLAG_DAMAGE_STEP, so the era version is activatable during damage calculation while the modern version is confined to the Damage Step before damage calculation. The attached condition is the same test in both — the goat's inline `Duel.GetCurrentPhase()~=PHASE_DAMAGE or not Duel.IsDamageCalculated()` is literally the body of aux.StatChangeDamageStepCondition — and the reset constant is the same bits expanded, so the activation window is the entire behavioural difference. Chronology of the window change is unresolved.
